# the contributor audit: unequal transport and exposed simplex-base budgets



* Sections 1--3 of `candidate a972493c7a264f4e`.
* All of `candidate 0e12a7390f0ce25f`.



## Unequal full-body coupling

The conditional quantile map now has derivative product b/a. Its normalized midpoint-law density is at most 1/v_* by the subset-product arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. That inequality includes the empty subset separately and is valid for every d>=1. Scaling the probability coupling by a gives exact first marginal volume on A, second marginal (a/b) volume on B, mass a and mean (g_A+g_B)/2. The closed-cap implication is pointwise and all halfspaces use the same coupling. Thus eta<=a/v_* on K, with no discarded positive-volume part of the full endpoint marginals.

The selected middle point is the actual centroid of K+2eta. Its denominator k+2a is correct; the source explicitly does not identify it with the unequal-volume mixed centroid. Its cap credit is bounded by the original endpoint caps because a/b<=1. Pure integer normals retain K and at least the smaller endpoint. The repaired uniform strictness from the all-d source passes to the depth infimum.

For d=2, the lower bound k>=(b+3a)/4 follows from sqrt(ab)>=a. The coefficient of k in c_*(k+2a)-(2/9)(k+a+b) is positive. Substitution gives exactly (c_*/4-5/18)b+(11c_*/4-7/18)a; the coefficient of b is negative. Its value at b=5a/3 is 2177a/614115>0. The denominator is always the original k+a+b. This proves the stated ratio window for every compatible middle body.

## Vertex and midpoint base 2 Delta_n

Every edge midpoint has only its two exposed edge endpoints and its own fiber available in a convex combination, so the stated midpoint containment is exact. Shrinking a larger endpoint about its own centroid gives a genuine subset, preserves that centroid and its compatibility, and provides one actual edge point. Restricting any full ambient normal to the edge times the continuous space either gives the usual affine cap or a constant restriction; both are covered. No lattice-changing affine transformation is used.

After normalizing the certificate B to one and sorting the vertex volumes, the complete-graph sum is at most v_1+sum_{j>=2}[v_j+(j-1)min(1,4/3-v_j)]. Each bracket is bounded by j-2/3, including j=2 where its high branch is constant. The resulting sharp coefficient is (3N^2-N+4)/6. The induction comparison with 2^(N-1) has exactly the printed difference (3N-1)(N-2)/6.

At N=4 equality forces v_3=v_4=1/3 and their incident edge volumes one, so at least one edge expression attains B and its strict actual depth estimate applies. For larger N the mass comparison is strict. The n=2 sharp numerical menu has exact actual realization by nested homothetic copies of one body: exposed vertices retain their assigned fibers; edge midpoint fibers cannot exceed the common largest body and already contain it. The ambient convex hull is full dimensional and has precisely the stated integer projection.

This is a failure of the listed scalar lower certificates, not an upper bound on actual depth or a counterexample to OC. The positive-volume assumption remains explicit. No intrinsic or missing-fiber extension is inferred.

## Added full audit of Section 4: PASS

The density-ceiling refinement rescales the same eta by theta and keeps the original source law exactly K+2theta eta'. The cap-root constraint has coefficients 2theta throughout. Applying the same three Fenchel multipliers gives D_theta<=A_d+theta X_d, with X_d=1+A_d/3-epsilon_d. The reserve is therefore exactly (1-theta)A_d/3+theta epsilon_d. The conversion back to captured and total masses uses (1+theta alpha)/s=U+theta Q+theta E-theta; no factor of theta is omitted. Jensen supplies the second Gamma_d and the denominator (1+2a/k)^d in the additional term. Finally X_d>=1 follows from the first two binomial terms, so epsilon_d<=A_d/3 and pure integer caps exceed the claimed refined right side. This is a finite-parameter bound at the same actual point, not a claim that this point solves arbitrary imbalance.
